mentl/67cd227:
Two deep fixes exposed by the DSP crucible compilation through full HM:

ROOT CAUSE 1: bind handler was overwriting env_with_primitives' canonical
type declarations with inferred types from memory.lux implementations. For
example, from_char_code is declared (Int) -> String in primitives, but
memory.lux's implementation returns an i32 pointer, so the checker inferred
(Int) -> Int and overwrote the primitive. This made `let a = from_char_code(65)`
have type TInt instead of TString, causing `a ++ b` to dispatch to list_concat.

Fix: bind handler in check.lux now checks is_builtin_reason on the existing
entry and skips overwriting when it finds Declared("builtin"). The primitive
annotations are the canonical types; the memory.lux implementations provide
the runtime behavior.

Verified: `let a = from_char_code(65); let b = from_char_code(66); a ++ b`
now produces the correct 2-byte string [65, 66] via str_concat dispatch.

ROOT CAUSE 2: escape_wat_string used chars() which splits by Unicode
codepoints in the Rust VM. For "█" (U+2588 = 9608), this produced one
"char" with codepoint 9608. hex_byte(9608) then computed hex_digit(9608/16)
= hex_digit(600) = from_char_code(87 + 600) = from_char_code(687) = ʯ
(U+02AF). THAT's where the mysterious `\ʯ8` came from in WAT data segments.

Fix: added byte_at(s, i) and byte_len(s) builtins to the Rust VM that
iterate UTF-8 bytes, not codepoints. The WAT emitter now uses these for
string escaping. In WASM, they compile to load_i8 and load_i32 respectively.
Added to env_with_primitives with types (String, Int) -> Int and (String) -> Int.

First real content for crates/input_touch. Lands the local-only
TouchState resource and the PreUpdate pipeline that consumes Bevy's
Touches into structured stick/throw signals. Per CONVENTIONS,
TouchState is never rolled back and never serialized — it's pure
local state that cycle 5 will quantize at the boundary into the
4-byte wire-format PlayerInput.

Cycle 1 — raw touch ingest:
  * TrackedTouch (id, start_pos, current_pos, start_frame).
  * apply_touch_events: bevy-free pure transition that consumes
    just_pressed / just_released / just_canceled / active iterators.
    Tested in isolation without a Bevy app fixture.
  * update_touch_state: PreUpdate system, thin shim that pulls
    iterators out of Res<Touches> and forwards to apply_touch_events.
  * Frame counter advances every frame (even with no touches) so
    later cycles can measure elapsed-frames-since-touch-start.
  * id-reuse guard: when Bevy reuses a touch id immediately after
    a release, we drop the stale entry and rebuild from the new
    start_pos rather than leaking the old origin.

Cycle 2 — floating virtual stick + radial deadzone:
  * Tunables: STICK_DEADZONE_INNER = 0.12, STICK_DEADZONE_SATURATION
    = 0.75, STICK_MAX_RADIUS_PX = 80.0. 12% inner kills resting-thumb
    jitter; 75% saturation means the user only has to drag 75% of
    the way to the virtual circle's edge to feel max push; 80px is
    the standard mobile thumb radius.
  * apply_radial_deadzone: linear remap [inner, saturation] -> [0, 1],
    clamped at both ends.
  * compute_stick: bevy-free; returns a [-1, 1]^2 vector after the
    deadzone curve, direction preserved.

    large y). Rejects zero-window inputs by construction so the
